question: An object is placed at distance of 20cm in front of a concave mirror and it’s image is formed at a distance of 60cm on the same side as the object, the magnification produced by the mirror will be:
solution:
The correct answer is __**-3**__

__**Concept:**__

**Concave Mirror:**

__
 
• A concave mirror is a spherical mirror with a reflecting surface that curves inward.
 
• The magnification (m) produced by a mirror is the ratio of the height of the image (hᵢ) to the height of the object (hₒ).
 
• m = (h_i)/(h_o)=-(v)/(u) 

**Calculation:**__

Given,

Object distance, u = -20 cm

Image distance, v = -60 cm

The magnification produced by the mirror is,

 m = -(v)/(u) 

⇒ m = -((-60)/(-20))

m = -3

**∴ The magnification produced by the mirror is -3.**
